paper_title: Searching for scalar field dark matter with LIGO
coupling_convention: Lambda_gamma^-1 in GeV^-1 (left axis of panel b), as plotted
notes: LIGO O3 search for scalar field dark matter via beamsplitter/test-mass size oscillations. Constrains both Lambda_gamma (d_e, ScalarPhoton coupling to photons/alpha) and Lambda_e (d_me, ScalarElectron coupling to electron mass), with the assumption that the other coupling is null. Frequency band 10-180 Hz corresponds to roughly 5e-14 to 1e-12 eV mass (paper states this). Limits are 95% C.L. assuming rho=0.4 GeV/cm^3. Numerical exclusion values are only available as smoothed curves in Fig. 3 (no data table), so no reliable (mass, coupling) pairs could be extracted. Coupling type is ambiguous between ScalarPhoton (Lambda_gamma/d_e) and ScalarElectron (Lambda_e/d_me) since both are reported. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Panel b) constrains Lambda_gamma^-1 (photon coupling, d_e on right axis = ScalarPhoton). The paper's own result is the thick blue line spanning ~10-180 Hz (5e-14 to 1e-12 eV). Emitted values are the LEFT-axis Lambda_gamma^-1 in GeV^-1 as plotted, NOT the dimensionless d_e. The minimum of the blue exclusion boundary is around Lambda_gamma^-1 ~ 1.6e-21 GeV^-1 near a few 1e-13 eV. Note: the plotted quantity is Lambda_gamma^-1 (GeV^-1), not the dimensionless d_e; if d_e values are required use the right axis instead.
